claims.statement: The roaster exploration flow is a three-level SvelteKit drill-down: /roasters (all-roasters listing with search + Grid/Sticker toggle) → /roasters/{roaster_name} (roaster detail) → /roasters/{roaster_name}/{bean_name} (bean detail page), with the roasted-in location tree as a location-first alternative entry point that feeds into both the listing and individual roaster detail pages.

The /roasters listing load calls api.getRoasters(fetch) which hits GET /v1/roasters; the backend joins roasters to coffee_beans for current_beans_count, decorates each roaster with hierarchical location_codes/country_slug/region_slug from the scraper registry, and caches the response in SimpleMemoryCache.

The roasters listing page renders a debounced (300ms) client-side search filtering roasters by name or location, a Grid/Stickers view toggle, a results summary, and an empty state offering to clear the search or suggest the typed query as a new roaster; continent quick-links point at /roasted-in/{slug} routes.

The Suggest a Roaster dialog merges implemented roasters with community suggestions in a combobox, deduplicates against both sets, submits via submitRoasterSuggestion, optimistically prepends the new suggestion on a 'created' result, calls invalidateAll to refetch, and requires a session for upvoting (redirecting to /login when anonymous).

RoasterCard is the grid tile showing the roaster's logo_sticker.png, name, location, a UTM-tagged website link, a relative last-updated timestamp derived from last_scraped, and an 'Explore N Beans' button deep-linking to /search?roaster={name}&apply_location_defaults=false; its location text links to /roasted-in/{region_slug}/{country_slug} when both slugs are present.

RoasterStickerWall (~27KB) is a physics-based collage of roaster logo stickers using a D3 force simulation (d3-force + d3-force-boundary) with forceX/forceY positioning, forceManyBody charge, and a forceCollide whose radius is STICKER_SIZE/2 + PADDING; stickers are absolutely-positioned divs translated by simulated x/y with a stable per-roaster rotation.

When a debounced search query is active, RoasterStickerWall pulls matched stickers into a centered horizontal band (stronger forceX/forceY), dims non-matches to opacity 0.1 and pushes them down, temporarily disables collision for matches so they float through each other, and re-enables collision after a 1s timeout.

RoasterStickerWall caches sticker positions in localStorage under a key hashed from sorted roaster IDs; on an exact width/height match with all positions known it snaps to cached positions and stops the simulation, and on a resize it scales cached positions proportionally and re-runs with a lower alpha.

RoasterStickerWall uses a Delaunay triangulation (delaunay.find) to hit-test mouse moves against stickers for hover; click pins a selectedRoaster whose tooltip stays open until dismissed or a window click clears it, and the pinned tooltip offers 'Explore N Beans' (deep-link to /search?roaster=...&apply_location_defaults=false) and a UTM-tagged 'Visit Website' link — it does not link directly to the roaster detail page.
RoasterStickerWall is reused by LocationLayout.svelte on the roasted-in pages, so the sticker view is consistent across the roasters listing and every location page.

The roaster detail load (+page.ts) calls api.getRoasterDetail(slug, currency, fetch) against GET /v1/roasters/{roaster_slug} with an optional convert_to_currency query, resolves the user's selected currency from the parent layout, and returns the roaster plus the full detail payload; a 404 whose message contains 'not found' is converted to a SvelteKit error(404).

The roaster detail load returns a deferred beans promise: beans and pagination are produced by api.search({ roaster: detail.name, page, per_page, sort_by, sort_order }) and consumed in the template via {#await beans}; sort and page changes update URL search params with replaceState + noScroll so the load re-runs without scrolling.

The roaster detail page renders, in order: breadcrumb + back button; a header card with logo, name, location with an iconify circle-flags flag derived from location_codes[0], and a website link; Awards badges when roaster.awards is non-empty; About description; the 'What Makes Them Unique' headline; Flavour Profile donut and Roast Profile bar (two-column when roast_distribution total >= 10, else donut alone); and a Coffee Beans grid with search, SortControls, and PaginationControls.

The roaster detail load returns statistics (total_beans, available_beans, avg_cupping_score, avg_price_usd, total_origins, total_varieties) and the top_origins, varietals, processing_methods, and common_tasting_notes distributions, but the current template does not render a numeric statistics panel or those distribution lists directly — the visible distribution visualisations are the flavour donut and the roast bar.

The uniqueness report is computed entirely in the backend by _compute_uniqueness_report and returned as RoasterDetailResponse.uniqueness; the frontend renders only the top insight as a two-sentence 'What Makes Them Unique' statement, with the section gated behind {#if uniquenessTop && uniquenessSentenceTop} so it is omitted when no dimension clears the backend thresholds.

The uniqueness headline adapts its wording per dimension via uniquenessSentence(): 'tasting notes skew' for flavour, 'sourcing skews' for origin, 'processing skews' for process, 'varietals skew' for varietal, followed by 'more so than {percentile}% of roasters'; the detail sentence reports this_roaster_pct vs global_pct with a signed lift and the sample_size, lowercasing flavour/process labels while keeping origin/varietal proper-case.

The roaster detail page prepares but does not currently render the secondary uniqueness dimension chips: uniquenessChips is derived from Object.values(data.uniqueness.by_dimension), a dimensionIcon() helper maps dimensions to lucide icons, and a DIMENSION_NOUN map is defined, but no chip markup iterating by_dimension is present in the template — only the single top headline is surfaced.

Each UniquenessInsight carries a link field providing an absolute site path to explore the standout category further (e.g. /origins/et for origin, /processes/{slug} for process, /varietals/{slug} for varietal; null for flavour), intended to round-trip into the dedicated exploration routes from the dimension chips.

The bean drill-down at /roasters/{roaster_name}/{bean_name} is loaded by +page.ts calling api.getBeanBySlug(roaster_name, bean_name, fetch, currency) against GET /v1/beans/{roaster_slug}/{bean_slug}, throwing a SvelteKit error(404) when the bean is not found and the roaster is not 'custom'; the 'custom' roaster slug is reserved for user-created beans stored in the local Dexie vault and hydrated client-side.

The roasted-in /roasted-in index redirects (301) to /roasters; a single slug /roasted-in/{slug} resolves to either a region (codes XE, EU, XA, XF, XN, XS, XO) or a country; the two-segment /roasted-in/{region_slug}/{country_slug} route verifies the hierarchy by fetching both via api.getLocationDetail and throws error(400, 'Invalid location hierarchy') if the country's location_type is not 'country' or the region's is not 'region'.

GET /v1/roaster-locations returns all roaster_location_codes with hierarchical roaster counts computed by walking the scraper registry, expanding each roaster's country to its hierarchical codes via get_hierarchical_location_codes, and counting any roaster whose expansion contains the code; regional codes (XE Europe, EU European Union) carry an included_countries list, and results are sorted by roaster count descending then location name.

GET /v1/roasted-in/{slug} resolves the slug via normalize_region_name to a location code, filters roasters hierarchically, and returns a LocationDetailResponse carrying statistics (available_beans, total_beans, roaster_count, city_count for countries, country_count for regions), top_roasters, top_cities, top_origins, varietals, and (for regions) countries; it is cached in SimpleMemoryCache.

LocationLayout.svelte is the shared shell for roasted-in pages: it renders breadcrumbs, a title, two stat cards (total beans linking to /search?roaster_location={code}, and roaster count), Popular Origins and Top Varietals insight cards with deep-links into search, a roaster search input, the same Grid/Stickers toggle as the roasters listing, and the roaster list via RoasterCard or RoasterStickerWall.

The roasted-in region page additionally renders a countries grid via the countriesSection snippet in [slug]/+page.svelte, where each country card shows its flag, bean and roaster counts, and links to /roasted-in/{region_slug}/{country_slug}.

The roaster detail page's FlavourProfileDonut renders flavour_categories as a layerchart PieChart donut, sorting slices by FLAVOUR_CATEGORY_ORDER and colouring them via getFlavourCategoryHexColor, with callout labels hidden for slices below 2% unless their arc is hovered.

The roaster detail page emits SEO metadata including a canonical URL, an OG image at /og/roaster/{roaster_name} (1200x630), and a Twitter card image, plus a meta description built from the roaster name and location.
